title: Review sequential awaits inside loops
why: Starting independent asynchronous work one iteration at a time can increase latency. Awaiting promises that have already started does not serialize their execution; ordering, backpressure, or isolated measurements may require sequential awaits.
suggestion: Use bounded concurrency only when iterations start independent work. Keep intentional ordering and backpressure; Promise.all aggregates promises but does not itself impose a concurrency limit.
limitations: Only lines beginning with await inside recognized braced loops are reported, with nested callback boundaries respected.

Infinite while (true) service loops, for-await stream consumers, explicit wait/backoff/delay/pause/sleep and Promise-based setTimeout calls, and direct once imports or const destructuring requires from events/node:events are excluded as sequential wait/backpressure contexts.

Other dependencies, ordering requirements and rate limits remain advisory review decisions. Event-wait suppression requires a real lexical import and only awaited direct uses outside that binding; any other same-name use, including shadowing, reassignment or an indirect reference, conservatively disables suppression throughout the file. Namespace aliases and arbitrary wrappers are not resolved. A nested finite loop is reviewed independently of an enclosing service loop; repeated evidence is grouped per file.

Collecting already-started promises does not start additional parallel work; benchmark isolation, shared graph traversal, protocol framing and wrapper-based stream waits can also require serialization. These remain contextual advice unless a recognized sequential form proves the intent.
